files.name: CHANGELOG.md
files.body:
### Added
- **`occ duplicates:list-all`, a read only report of the duplicates of all users, for the administrator** (Fix [#195](https://github.com/eldertek/duplicatefinder/issues/195), follow-up of [#155](https://github.com/eldertek/duplicatefinder/issues/155)). It groups the indexed files by content hash whoever owns them and prints, for each group, the hash, the size, the number of copies, the space wasted by the extra copies, and the owner and path of every copy. The biggest waste comes first, so the old Debian ISOs that three users keep are at the top. Options: `--min-size` (bytes or a unit: `500K`, `10M`, `1G`), `--limit` (100 groups by default, `0` for all of them) and `--output=table|json`. Running `occ` needs access to the server, so the report is reserved to the administrator, and the web interface keeps showing every user only the files he can access. The command only reads the table of the indexed files: it deletes nothing, writes nothing, and scans or hashes nothing. It reads the hashes the app has already stored, so the users that have never been scanned (no indexed file) are named at the end of the report (`users_without_index` in the JSON), and `occ duplicates:find-all --user=NAME` indexes them. Ignored files, files without a hash and empty files (they waste no space) are left out. Measured on Nextcloud 35.0.1 with SQLite, MariaDB 12.3 and PostgreSQL 18, and on a table of 1.5 million rows with a memory limit of 96 MB (47 000 groups listed in under two minutes)
- Unit tests of the command (table, JSON, limit, minimum size, users never scanned, bad options, and the proof that it never writes)
